text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: sustained P95 latency breach on /v1/chat.generate in us-west-2. Threshold 900ms, observed ~1.6s for 9m. Severity: high. Trigger: synthetic + customer signal (acct-9201).
oncall-rita: on-call rita. pulling dashboards and traces now. starting canonical thread for timeline + hypotheses.
leo: p50 stayed ~300ms, p95 jumped from ~420ms -> ~1.6s at ~11:08 UTC. No error rate increase.
max: grabbing flamegraphs and perf counters on redwood-runtime processes on worker nodes. initial glance shows increased kernel preempt_time and softirq stall counts.
eng-perf: searching traces: many long spans labeled `scheduler_wait` and `cpu_preempt` between enqueue -> start_execute. sample trace: trace-id tr-b7f6c3, spans: submit(8ms) -> scheduler_wait(980ms) -> context_switch(420ms) -> model_infer(12ms). link: https://traces.internal/tr-b7f6c3 (sanitized).
ops-kim: any infra change in region? deploy-bot: infra:kernel-rollout by max at 10:50 UTC (kernel-5.16.4+preempt).
max: confirmed kernel promotion at 10:50 (canary -> region). change includes scheduler preemption backports.
oncall-rita: hypotheses: H1 kernel preempt/scheduler patch causing long tail; H2 runtime batching deadlock; H3 node-level hostd resource saturation causing stalls.
leo: runtime logs show repeated messages: ```
[11:08:29] runtime: blocked acquiring scheduling token (held 310ms)
[11:08:29] runtime: processed req id=xy-9 elapsed=1580ms
```
eng-perf: perf stat summary (host rwd-w2-05): ```
Performance counter stats for '10s':
  context-switches: 1,800,456
  cpu-migrations: 23,412
  voluntary_context_switches: 1,600,123
```
ops-kim: rolling mitigation options: A) route 30% traffic to us-east-1, B) rollback kernel on small cohort, C) bump batcher concurrency and cap idle time.
deploy-bot: routing policy applied: 30% shift to us-east-1 at 11:25 UTC.
oncall-rita: choose quick mitigation now: route traffic + start kernel rollback on 4 hosts as canary. max, please kick off rollback.
max: rolling back kernel to 5.16.2 on 4 canary hosts (rwd-w2-05..08). job id rb-20260315-02. monitoring.
tracebot: captured trace tr-b7f6c3 and uploaded heap/trace to /s3/trace-dumps/1918804321-tr-b7f6c3.json.gz
leo: after canary rollback p95 on canaries dropped from ~1.6s -> ~420ms within 6m. non-rolled hosts still high. signal points to H1.
eng-perf: pre-rollback vs post-canary counters: pre ctx-switches 1.8M, post-canary 520k. sys time proportion reduced.
ops-kim: customer acct-9201 notified: "We saw degradation earlier; mitigation in place and rollback underway. We'll update when fully remediated."
max: starting phased rollback for remaining hosts in region. ETA full completion 30m. job id rb-20260315-03.
eng-perf: bisect plan: reproduce in perf lab with same request mix, apply subset of scheduler patches, measure scheduler_wait and context_switch counters. suspect commit range: scheduler/fairness backports 3-7.
leo: commands/logs we used: ```
# sample traces
curl -s "https://api.internal/v1/traces?trace_id=tr-b7f6c3" > /tmp/trb7.json
# perf sample
ssh ops@rwd-w2-05 "sudo perf stat -e context-switches,cpu-migrations,cs -p $(pgrep redwood-runtime) sleep 10"
# runtime logs
journalctl -u redwood-runtime --since '2026-03-15 10:45' --until '2026-03-15 11:50' | grep -E 'blocked|kv-cache' | tail -n 150
```
eng-perf: long-running span breakdown analysis: majority of tail time is scheduler_wait -> context_switch -> kernel call, model execution time is tiny. points away from model or GPU stalls.
oncall-rita: hypothesis tracker: H1 (kernel scheduler regress) = supported by perf + rollback signal. H2 (runtime batching) = inconclusive; will run targeted stress test. H3 (host saturation) = unlikely; CPU usage normal.
sre-bot: incident created INC-2026-0315-LATREG-02. severity scaled down to medium at 12:10 UTC after region rollback.
max: rollback completed for all hosts at 12:05 UTC. region p95 back to ~430ms and stable.
ops-kim: follow-ups: - bisect kernel commits (max + eng-perf), - add pre-deploy perf smoke to rollout pipeline (leo + eng-perf), - update runbook for similar rollouts (rita + ops).
oncall-rita: timeline (canonical): 10:50 UTC kernel rollout -> 11:08 UTC p95 spike detected -> 11:25 UTC traffic shift started -> 11:30 UTC canary rollback initiated -> 11:36 UTC canary p95 improved -> 12:05 UTC region rollback complete -> 12:10 UTC severity downgrade.
eng-perf: immediate next action: reproduce on perf harness and bisect down to offending patch. I'll post repro steps and trace links here.
tracebot: artifacts: /s3/trace-dumps/1918804321-tr-b7f6c3.json.gz, /s3/perf-reports/1918804321-canary-pre.txt, /s3/perf-reports/1918804321-canary-post.txt
oncall-rita: assigning owners: max (rollback & bisect lead), eng-perf (perf analysis & repro), leo (dashboards + alert tuning), rita (postmortem & runbook). keeping thread as canonical incident conversation.
ops-kim: customer comms: status page updated, support notified impacted customers.
eng-perf: open questions: 1) which scheduler subpatch introduced preempt delay? 2) why did preemption cause such high context-switch counts? 3) can we add a quick perf smoke to detect this in future rollouts?
oncall-rita: great work team. closing active mitigation. leaving thread open for RCA updates and bisect results. (reacji :white_check_mark:)
